A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same MedRaC study, with complete methods, experiments, figures, tables and appendix material. Content can be matched despite pagination changes and the reorganization of prompt templates into Appendix H.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations on 940 retained MedCalc-Bench cases, human annotation agreement, component ablations and retrieval experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these original benchmark, human annotation, ablation and retrieval results.

M1.justification: The Formula-RAG and Python execution pipeline, four-stage evaluation procedure and evaluator prompt contents are unchanged. The reformatted prompt appendix introduces no new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same cleaned MedCalc-Bench cases, rule-based and equation-based tasks, specialty coverage, and retrieval experiments with 55 and 785 formulas.

E2.justification: Direct prompting, CoT, One-shot, Self-Refine and MedPrompt retain identical participation in the corresponding comparisons. The changed MedPrompt citation does not change its documented implementation or comparator membership.

E3.justification: The 940-case evaluation, 46-case human study, scoring tolerances, model configurations, k=3 MedPrompt retrieval and maximum five Self-Refine rounds are unchanged.

E4.justification: The RAG and code ablations, retrieval scaling analysis, specialty comparisons, error-type analyses and sodium-correction case study are retained. Their relocation adds no new analysis.

E5.justification: The reporting practices are unchanged. Neither version provides seed counts, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals or significance tests; the same agreement calculations are retained.

E6.justification: Every entry in Tables 1–9 matches. For example, Table 1 retains GPT-4o MedRaC accuracies of 51.03% for rule-based tasks and 64.39% for calculations. Figure results and case-study findings also remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 retains the same step-dependence assumption and definitions of overall correctness, Conditional Correctness and First Error Attribution Rate. No mathematical argument or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: revised medical-calculation evaluation, structured error attribution and training-free MedRaC enhancement. Their quantitative headline claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: The interpretations of retrieval and code benefits, clinical interpretation bottlenecks and model-size effects are unchanged. The limitations concerning structured English tasks, curated notes, LLM judges and accurate formula banks are also retained.

D1.justification: Data exclusions, annotation instructions, two RTX A6000 GPUs, decoding settings and evaluator identities remain unchanged. The same code/data access information, Apache-2.0 license and prompt contents are retained; only their presentation changes.

R1.justification: The healthcare RAG survey citation changes from Miao et al. to Amugongo et al. (2025), and the MedPrompt reference changes from Nori et al. (2023b) to 'From medprompt to o1' (2024). Other edits largely update metadata for matched works. The substantive research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The main prose and section sequence remain stable. Prompt Templates becomes numbered Appendix H, with H.1/H.2 and H.2.x replacing unnumbered headings and G.0.x labels. Bibliographic wording is revised and the EMNLP acceptance footnote is removed.

P2.justification: Existing displays are rearranged: the appendix error plots form a single column, and Tables 8–9 share a page. Prompt listings receive black title bars, enclosing boxes and different wrapping. Printed page numbers disappear. The figures and table contents themselves are unchanged.

improvement.justification: V2 preserves the methods, evidence, interpretations and reproducibility content. Appendix H's clearer hierarchy and titled prompt boxes improve organization, while increased listing fragmentation and missing printed page numbers reduce convenience. These limited presentation tradeoffs and reference edits leave overall paper quality essentially unchanged.
